/-!
# Zariski's multiplicity conjecture

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics lists the "Zariski multiplicity conjecture
on the topological equisingularity and equimultiplicity of varieties at singular points".

Zariski's multiplicity conjecture is the question of whether the multiplicity of a complex
hypersurface singularity is an invariant of its embedded topological type (Zariski's Question A),
and whether topological equisingularity of a hypersurface along a nonsingular subvariety implies
equimultiplicity along it (Zariski's Question B, a weaker form implied by Question A). Both were
posed by Zariski in 1971 and remain open in general. Despite the word "varieties" in the list
entry, the conjecture concerns hypersurfaces. Solved special cases ($n = 2$, multiplicity one,
$C^1$ or bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms) are not stated here.

Here a *hypersurface* $V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ near a point $P$ is the zero set of a holomorphic
function $F$ which is *reduced* at $P$, i.e. whose germ at $P$ is square-free in the ring of
holomorphic germs. The *multiplicity* $m(V, P)$ of $V$ at $P$ is the order of $F$ at $P$, i.e. the
degree of the lowest-degree non-zero homogeneous term in the Taylor expansion of $F$ at $P$. The
reducedness hypothesis is essential: $f$ and $f^2$ define the same zero set.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Algebraic variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/algebraic_variety)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Za71] Zariski, O. *Some open questions in the theory of singularities*.
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 77 (1971), 481–491.
- [Ey07] Eyral, C. *Zariski's multiplicity question — a survey*.
  New Zealand J. Math. 36 (2007), 253–276.
-/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def orderAt (f : E → ℂ) (p : E) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k f p ≠ 0}
blocks.docstring:
The order of a function `f : E → ℂ` at a point `p`: the least `k` such that the `k`-th
derivative of `f` at `p` is non-zero. For a holomorphic `f` which does not vanish identically
near `p`, this is the degree of the lowest-degree non-zero homogeneous term of the Taylor
expansion of `f` at `p`, i.e. the multiplicity at `p` of the hypersurface defined by `f` when
`f` is reduced at `p`. It takes the junk value `0` if `f` vanishes identically near `p`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `analyticOrderAt` / `analyticOrderNatAt` (only for f : 𝕜 → E, one variable); `FormalMultilinearSeries.order` (not well-defined on the function since multivariable power series are not unique; p n ≠ 0 does not imply the homogeneous part is nonzero).
justification.name: Varieties.orderAt
justification.why_needed: The multiplicity/order of vanishing of a holomorphic function of several variables at a point: sInf {k | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k f p ≠ 0}. For analytic f not identically zero near p this is the degree of the lowest non-zero homogeneous Taylor term (iteratedFDeriv is symmetric, so it detects the homogeneous part; char 0 polarization). Junk value 0 for the zero germ, which is excluded by reducedness in both theorems.

blocks.name: orderAt
blocks.text:
/-- The order of a function `f : E → ℂ` at a point `p`: the least `k` such that the `k`-th
derivative of `f` at `p` is non-zero. For a holomorphic `f` which does not vanish identically
near `p`, this is the degree of the lowest-degree non-zero homogeneous term of the Taylor
expansion of `f` at `p`, i.e. the multiplicity at `p` of the hypersurface defined by `f` when
`f` is reduced at `p`. It takes the junk value `0` if `f` vanishes identically near `p`. -/
noncomputable def orderAt (f : E → ℂ) (p : E) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k f p ≠ 0}

blocks.docstring:
A function `f : E → ℂ` is *reduced* at `p` if its germ at `p` is square-free in the ring
of germs of holomorphic functions at `p`, i.e. whenever `f` agrees near `p` with `g ^ 2 * h` for
holomorphic `g` and `h`, the factor `g` is a unit, that is `g p ≠ 0`. In particular `f` does not
vanish identically near `p`. This is meant to be applied to functions holomorphic at `p`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Squarefree` / `IsReduced` — but Mathlib has no ring of analytic germs (`Filter.Germ` exists but no analytic subring), so they cannot be applied directly.
justification.name: Varieties.IsReducedAt
justification.why_needed: Reducedness of a holomorphic germ (square-free in the ring of holomorphic germs 𝒪_{ℂⁿ,p}): ∀ g h analytic at p, f =ᶠ[𝓝 p] g^2 * h → g p ≠ 0. This is exactly Mathlib's `Squarefree` (∀ x, x*x ∣ f → IsUnit x) transported to the germ ring, where units are germs with g p ≠ 0; it also excludes the zero germ. Tests: id is reduced, z^2 and 0 are not.

blocks.name: IsReducedAt
blocks.text:
/-- A function `f : E → ℂ` is *reduced* at `p` if its germ at `p` is square-free in the ring
of germs of holomorphic functions at `p`, i.e. whenever `f` agrees near `p` with `g ^ 2 * h` for
holomorphic `g` and `h`, the factor `g` is a unit, that is `g p ≠ 0`. In particular `f` does not
vanish identically near `p`. This is meant to be applied to functions holomorphic at `p`. -/
def IsReducedAt (f : E → ℂ) (p : E) : Prop :=
  ∀ g h : E → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g p → AnalyticAt ℂ h p →
    (f =ᶠ[𝓝 p] fun x => g x ^ 2 * h x) → g p ≠ 0

@[category test, AMS 14 32]
theorem orderAt_id : orderAt (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 = 1 := by
  have h0 : 0 ∉ {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 ≠ 0} := by
    simp [iteratedFDeriv_zero_eq_comp]
  have h1 : 1 ∈ {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 ≠ 0} := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ne_eq]
    intro h
    have := congrArg (fun T => T (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))) h
    simp [iteratedFDeriv_one_apply] at this
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le h1) ?_
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
  intro h
  exact h0 (h ▸ Nat.sInf_mem ⟨1, h1⟩)
blocks.docstring: The order of the identity function of `ℂ` at `0` is `1`.

theorem isReducedAt_id : IsReducedAt (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 := by
  intro g h hg hh hfg hg0
  have := hfg.deriv_eq
  rw [deriv_id'', deriv_fun_mul (hg.differentiableAt.fun_pow 2) hh.differentiableAt,
    deriv_fun_pow hg.differentiableAt 2] at this
  simp [hg0] at this

theorem not_isReducedAt_sq : ¬ IsReducedAt (fun z : ℂ => z ^ 2) 0 := by
  intro H
  exact H (fun z => z) (fun _ => 1) analyticAt_id analyticAt_const
    (by filter_upwards with z; simp) rfl

def IsSmoothSubvarietyAt {n : ℕ} (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ)
    (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ ψ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))),
    P ∈ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ.symm ψ.target ∧
      ∀ x ∈ ψ.source, x ∈ W ↔ (ψ x).2 = 0
blocks.docstring:
A set `W ⊆ ℂⁿ` is a *nonsingular (complex-analytic) subvariety of dimension `d`* near a
point `P ∈ W` if there is a biholomorphic chart of a neighbourhood of `P` in `ℂⁿ` onto an open
subset of `ℂ^d × ℂ^(n - d)` which carries `W` onto the linear subspace `ℂ^d × {0}`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has no notion of (complex) submanifold of a normed space; `IsImmersion`/`ChartedSpace` do not describe a subset of ℂⁿ being a submanifold.
justification.name: Varieties.IsSmoothSubvarietyAt
justification.why_needed: W ⊆ ℂⁿ is a nonsingular complex-analytic subvariety of dimension d near P: existence of an `OpenPartialHomeomorph` ψ from a neighbourhood of P onto an open subset of ℂ^d × ℂ^(n-d), analytic with analytic inverse (`AnalyticOnNhd`), with x ∈ W ↔ (ψ x).2 = 0 on the source. Standard definition of an embedded complex submanifold.

/-- A set `W ⊆ ℂⁿ` is a *nonsingular (complex-analytic) subvariety of dimension `d`* near a

subset of `ℂ^d × ℂ^(n - d)` which carries `W` onto the linear subspace `ℂ^d × {0}`. -/
def IsSmoothSubvarietyAt {n : ℕ} (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ)
    (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ ψ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))),
    P ∈ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ.symm ψ.target ∧
      ∀ x ∈ ψ.source, x ∈ W ↔ (ψ x).2 = 0

def IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong {n : ℕ} (F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ)
    (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ) (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))))
    (U₁ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d))) (U₂ S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d)))),
    P ∈ h.source ∧ h.target = U₁ ×ˢ U₂ ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, x ∈ W ↔ (h x).2 = 0) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, F x = 0 ↔ (h x).2 ∈ S)
blocks.docstring:
The hypersurface `V = {F = 0} ⊆ ℂⁿ` is *topologically equisingular* along the
`d`-dimensional subvariety `W` at the point `P ∈ W` if the triple `(ℂⁿ, V, W)` is locally
topologically trivial along `W` at `P`: there is a homeomorphism `h` from a neighbourhood `U` of
`P` in `ℂⁿ` onto a product `U₁ × U₂` of open sets `U₁ ⊆ ℂ^d`, `U₂ ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` such that
`h (W ∩ U) = U₁ × {0}` and `h (V ∩ U) = U₁ × S` for some set `S ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` (so that `S ∩ U₂`
is homeomorphic to a transversal slice of `V`). Such an `h` yields, for every `Q ∈ W ∩ U`, a
homeomorphism between neighbourhoods of `Q` and `P` in `ℂⁿ` carrying `V` onto `V` and `Q` to `P`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib/FormalConjecturesForMathlib describes local topological triviality of a pair along a subvariety; `IsImage`/`OpenPartialHomeomorph` are only building blocks.
justification.name: Varieties.IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong
justification.why_needed: Zariski's topological equisingularity of V = {F = 0} along W at P (ambient local topological triviality): an `OpenPartialHomeomorph` h from a neighbourhood U of P onto a product U₁ ×ˢ U₂ ⊆ ℂ^d × ℂ^(n-d) with h(W ∩ U) = U₁ × {0} (x ∈ W ↔ (h x).2 = 0) and h(V ∩ U) = U₁ × S (F x = 0 ↔ (h x).2 ∈ S) for some set S. This yields ambient homeomorphisms (ℂⁿ, V, Q) → (ℂⁿ, V, P) for all Q ∈ W ∩ U, so the slot is implied by Question A, as the decomposition requires.

blocks.name: IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong
blocks.text:
/-- The hypersurface `V = {F = 0} ⊆ ℂⁿ` is *topologically equisingular* along the
`d`-dimensional subvariety `W` at the point `P ∈ W` if the triple `(ℂⁿ, V, W)` is locally
topologically trivial along `W` at `P`: there is a homeomorphism `h` from a neighbourhood `U` of
`P` in `ℂⁿ` onto a product `U₁ × U₂` of open sets `U₁ ⊆ ℂ^d`, `U₂ ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` such that
`h (W ∩ U) = U₁ × {0}` and `h (V ∩ U) = U₁ × S` for some set `S ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` (so that `S ∩ U₂`
is homeomorphic to a transversal slice of `V`). Such an `h` yields, for every `Q ∈ W ∩ U`, a
homeomorphism between neighbourhoods of `Q` and `P` in `ℂⁿ` carrying `V` onto `V` and `Q` to `P`.
-/
def IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong {n : ℕ} (F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ)
    (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ) (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))))
    (U₁ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d))) (U₂ S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d)))),
    P ∈ h.source ∧ h.target = U₁ ×ˢ U₂ ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, x ∈ W ↔ (h x).2 = 0) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, F x = 0 ↔ (h x).2 ∈ S)

@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties {n : ℕ} {f g : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f 0) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g 0) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) (hg₀ : g 0 = 0)
    (hf' : IsReducedAt f 0) (hg' : IsReducedAt g 0)
    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)))
    (h₀ : 0 ∈ φ.source) (hφ₀ : φ 0 = 0)
    (hφ : ∀ x ∈ φ.source, f x = 0 ↔ g (φ x) = 0) :
    orderAt f 0 = orderAt g 0 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Zariski's multiplicity conjecture** (Zariski's Question A, [Za71]).

Let $f, g : (\mathbb{C}^n, 0) \to (\mathbb{C}, 0)$ be reduced holomorphic function germs, and
suppose that the hypersurface germs $(V(f), 0)$ and $(V(g), 0)$ have the same embedded
topological type, i.e. there is a homeomorphism $\varphi$ between open neighbourhoods of $0$ in
$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $\varphi(0) = 0$ carrying $V(f)$ onto $V(g)$. Then $f$ and $g$ have the same
multiplicity (order of vanishing) at $0$.

Here `φ` is an open partial homeomorphism of `ℂⁿ` whose source and target are neighbourhoods of
`0`; the hypothesis `hφ` says exactly that `φ` maps `V(f) ∩ φ.source` onto `V(g) ∩ φ.target`.
The reducedness hypotheses are essential: `f` and `f ^ 2` define the same zero set.

/-- **Zariski's multiplicity conjecture** (Zariski's Question A, [Za71]).

Let $f, g : (\mathbb{C}^n, 0) \to (\mathbb{C}, 0)$ be reduced holomorphic function germs, and
suppose that the hypersurface germs $(V(f), 0)$ and $(V(g), 0)$ have the same embedded
topological type, i.e. there is a homeomorphism $\varphi$ between open neighbourhoods of $0$ in
$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $\varphi(0) = 0$ carrying $V(f)$ onto $V(g)$. Then $f$ and $g$ have the same
multiplicity (order of vanishing) at $0$.

Here `φ` is an open partial homeomorphism of `ℂⁿ` whose source and target are neighbourhoods of
`0`; the hypothesis `hφ` says exactly that `φ` maps `V(f) ∩ φ.source` onto `V(g) ∩ φ.target`.
The reducedness hypotheses are essential: `f` and `f ^ 2` define the same zero set. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties {n : ℕ} {f g : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f 0) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g 0) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) (hg₀ : g 0 = 0)
    (hf' : IsReducedAt f 0) (hg' : IsReducedAt g 0)
    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)))
    (h₀ : 0 ∈ φ.source) (hφ₀ : φ 0 = 0)
    (hφ : ∀ x ∈ φ.source, f x = 0 ↔ g (φ x) = 0) :
    orderAt f 0 = orderAt g 0 := by
  sorry

@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties.variants.equisingular_family {n d : ℕ} {F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    {W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))} {P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)}
    (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F P) (hF₀ : F P = 0) (hF' : IsReducedAt F P)
    (hP : P ∈ W) (hW : IsSmoothSubvarietyAt W d P)
    (hV : IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong F W d P) :
    ∀ᶠ Q in 𝓝[W] P, orderAt F Q = orderAt F P := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity** (Zariski's Question B, [Za71]),
a consequence of `Varieties.varieties`.

Let $V = \{F = 0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a hypersurface with $F$ holomorphic and reduced at
$P \in V$, and let $W$ be a nonsingular subvariety of dimension $d$ through $P$. If $V$ is
topologically equisingular along $W$ at $P$, then $V$ is equimultiple along $W$ at $P$: the
multiplicity $m(V, Q)$ is constant for $Q \in W$ near $P$.

Topological equisingularity is taken in the sense of ambient local topological triviality of the
triple $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, W)$ along $W$ (see `IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong`), which is
stronger than asking that the germs $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, Q)$ have the same embedded topological
type for all $Q \in W$ near $P$. Topological equisingularity along $W$ together with $P \in V$
forces $W \subset V$ near $P$, so $W$ is a nonsingular subvariety of $V$ as in Zariski's
formulation. The conclusion is stated for `Q` in a neighbourhood of `P` in `W`, on which `F` is
holomorphic and reduced, so that `orderAt F Q` is the multiplicity of `V` at `Q`.
blocks.name: varieties.variants.equisingular_family
blocks.text:
/-- **Topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity** (Zariski's Question B, [Za71]),
a consequence of `Varieties.varieties`.

Let $V = \{F = 0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a hypersurface with $F$ holomorphic and reduced at
$P \in V$, and let $W$ be a nonsingular subvariety of dimension $d$ through $P$. If $V$ is
topologically equisingular along $W$ at $P$, then $V$ is equimultiple along $W$ at $P$: the
multiplicity $m(V, Q)$ is constant for $Q \in W$ near $P$.

Topological equisingularity is taken in the sense of ambient local topological triviality of the
triple $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, W)$ along $W$ (see `IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong`), which is
stronger than asking that the germs $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, Q)$ have the same embedded topological
type for all $Q \in W$ near $P$. Topological equisingularity along $W$ together with $P \in V$
forces $W \subset V$ near $P$, so $W$ is a nonsingular subvariety of $V$ as in Zariski's
formulation. The conclusion is stated for `Q` in a neighbourhood of `P` in `W`, on which `F` is
holomorphic and reduced, so that `orderAt F Q` is the multiplicity of `V` at `Q`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties.variants.equisingular_family {n d : ℕ} {F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    {W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))} {P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)}
    (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F P) (hF₀ : F P = 0) (hF' : IsReducedAt F P)
    (hP : P ∈ W) (hW : IsSmoothSubvarietyAt W d P)
    (hV : IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong F W d P) :
    ∀ᶠ Q in 𝓝[W] P, orderAt F Q = orderAt F P := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Zariski's Question A (1971): for reduced holomorphic germs f, g : (ℂⁿ,0) → (ℂ,0), if there is a homeomorphism φ between neighbourhoods of 0 in ℂⁿ with φ(0)=0 and φ(V(f)) = V(g) (same embedded topological type, ambient homeomorphism not merely of V(f) ≅ V(g)), then ord₀ f = ord₀ g; despite the entry's word 'varieties' the conjecture is for hypersurfaces, 'reduced' is essential (f vs f² is otherwise a trivial counterexample), and solved special cases (n = 2, multiplicity 1, C¹ or bi-Lipschitz φ) are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: Zariski's Question A stated with reduced (square-free germ) holomorphic f, g : (ℂⁿ,0) → (ℂ,0), an ambient OpenPartialHomeomorph φ with 0 ∈ source, φ 0 = 0 and φ(V(f) ∩ U) = V(g) ∩ U' (∀ x ∈ source, f x = 0 ↔ g (φ x) = 0), concluding ord₀ f = ord₀ g with ord = least k with iteratedFDeriv ℂ k f 0 ≠ 0 (intrinsic; the junk value 0 is unreachable since reducedness excludes the zero germ). c03/c05/c07 are essentially identical and would also have been acceptable; c08 chosen so both slots share one set of bespoke definitions and it has proved test lemmas. c02 is rejected: it quantifies over arbitrary (non-symmetric) FormalMultilinearSeries p with HasFPowerSeriesAt f p 0 and asserts p.order = q.order, which is false for n ≥ 2 (an antisymmetric degree-2 term can be added to p without changing the sums). c01's diagonalOrder is well-defined but no better; c04/c06 are fine but their slot-2 companions were not chosen.

claims.decomposer_note: Zariski's Question B, a weaker form implied by the primary: if a reduced hypersurface V ⊂ ℂⁿ is topologically equisingular along a smooth subvariety W through P (i.e. locally topologically trivial along W: a family of ambient homeomorphisms carrying (ℂⁿ, V, Q) to (ℂⁿ, V, P) for Q ∈ W near P, equivalently a topologically trivial one-parameter family f_t), then the multiplicity m(V,Q) is constant for Q ∈ W near P; the notion of topological equisingularity must be fixed as ambient topological triviality, not the weaker pointwise-same-topological-type.
claims.reviewer_why: Zariski's Question B in Zariski's own shape: V = {F = 0} with F holomorphic and reduced at P ∈ V, W an arbitrary set required to be a nonsingular d-dimensional analytic subvariety through P (biholomorphic straightening chart), and topological equisingularity fixed as ambient local topological triviality of the triple (ℂⁿ, V, W): a homeomorphism from a neighbourhood U of P onto a product U₁ × U₂ with h(W ∩ U) = U₁ × {0} and h(V ∩ U) = U₁ × S. Conclusion ∀ᶠ Q in 𝓝[W] P, ord_Q F = ord_P F, i.e. the hypersurface multiplicity m(V,Q) is constant along W near P, exactly as Zariski's 'equimultiple along W at P'. This is implied by Question A (translate in the U₁ factor conjugated by h) and implies the transversal-section (c03/c07) and fiber-preserving family (c05) variants, and it excludes the pointwise-same-type reading. c01/c04/c06 instead conclude constancy of the fiber multiplicity ord₀ f_t, which is a different quantity from m(V,(t,0)) in Zariski's question, and c01/c06 additionally demand product neighbourhoods on both sides (non-standard); c02 has the ill-defined p.order problem. Docstrings lightly edited.

Algebraic varieties are the central objects of study in algebraic geometry, a sub-field of mathematics. Classically, an algebraic variety is defined as the set of solutions of a system of polynomial equations over the real or complex numbers. Modern definitions generalize this concept in several different ways, while attempting to preserve the geometric intuition behind the original definition. 
Conventions regarding the definition of an algebraic variety differ slightly. For example, some definitions require an algebraic variety to be irreducible, which means that it is not the union of two smaller sets that are closed in the Zariski topology. Under this definition, non-irreducible algebraic varieties are called algebraic sets. Other conventions do not require irreducibility.
The fundamental theorem of algebra establishes a link between algebra and geometry by showing that a monic polynomial (an algebraic object) in one variable with complex number coefficients is determined by the set of its roots (a geometric object) in the complex plane. Generalizing this result, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz provides a fundamental correspondence between ideals of polynomial rings and algebraic sets. Using the Nullstellensatz and related results, mathematicians have established a strong correspondence between questions on algebraic sets and questions of ring theory. This correspondence is a defining feature of algebraic geometry.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zariski's multiplicity conjecture

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems in mathematics lists the "Zariski multiplicity conjecture
on the topological equisingularity and equimultiplicity of varieties at singular points".

Zariski's multiplicity conjecture is the question of whether the multiplicity of a complex
hypersurface singularity is an invariant of its embedded topological type (Zariski's Question A),
and whether topological equisingularity of a hypersurface along a nonsingular subvariety implies
equimultiplicity along it (Zariski's Question B, a weaker form implied by Question A). Both were
posed by Zariski in 1971 and remain open in general. Despite the word "varieties" in the list
entry, the conjecture concerns hypersurfaces. Solved special cases ($n = 2$, multiplicity one,
$C^1$ or bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms) are not stated here.

Here a *hypersurface* $V \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ near a point $P$ is the zero set of a holomorphic
function $F$ which is *reduced* at $P$, i.e. whose germ at $P$ is square-free in the ring of
holomorphic germs. The *multiplicity* $m(V, P)$ of $V$ at $P$ is the order of $F$ at $P$, i.e. the
degree of the lowest-degree non-zero homogeneous term in the Taylor expansion of $F$ at $P$. The
reducedness hypothesis is essential: $f$ and $f^2$ define the same zero set.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Algebraic variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/algebraic_variety)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Za71] Zariski, O. *Some open questions in the theory of singularities*.
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 77 (1971), 481–491.
- [Ey07] Eyral, C. *Zariski's multiplicity question — a survey*.
  New Zealand J. Math. 36 (2007), 253–276.
-/

open Topology Filter

namespace Varieties

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]

/-- The order of a function `f : E → ℂ` at a point `p`: the least `k` such that the `k`-th
derivative of `f` at `p` is non-zero. For a holomorphic `f` which does not vanish identically
near `p`, this is the degree of the lowest-degree non-zero homogeneous term of the Taylor
expansion of `f` at `p`, i.e. the multiplicity at `p` of the hypersurface defined by `f` when
`f` is reduced at `p`. It takes the junk value `0` if `f` vanishes identically near `p`. -/
noncomputable def orderAt (f : E → ℂ) (p : E) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k f p ≠ 0}

/-- A function `f : E → ℂ` is *reduced* at `p` if its germ at `p` is square-free in the ring
of germs of holomorphic functions at `p`, i.e. whenever `f` agrees near `p` with `g ^ 2 * h` for
holomorphic `g` and `h`, the factor `g` is a unit, that is `g p ≠ 0`. In particular `f` does not
vanish identically near `p`. This is meant to be applied to functions holomorphic at `p`. -/
def IsReducedAt (f : E → ℂ) (p : E) : Prop :=
  ∀ g h : E → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g p → AnalyticAt ℂ h p →
    (f =ᶠ[𝓝 p] fun x => g x ^ 2 * h x) → g p ≠ 0

/-- The order of the identity function of `ℂ` at `0` is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 32]
theorem orderAt_id : orderAt (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 = 1 := by
  have h0 : 0 ∉ {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 ≠ 0} := by
    simp [iteratedFDeriv_zero_eq_comp]
  have h1 : 1 ∈ {k : ℕ | iteratedFDeriv ℂ k (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 ≠ 0} := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ne_eq]
    intro h
    have := congrArg (fun T => T (fun _ => (1 : ℂ))) h
    simp [iteratedFDeriv_one_apply] at this
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le h1) ?_
  rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
  intro h
  exact h0 (h ▸ Nat.sInf_mem ⟨1, h1⟩)

/-- The identity function of `ℂ` is reduced at `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 32]
theorem isReducedAt_id : IsReducedAt (fun z : ℂ => z) 0 := by
  intro g h hg hh hfg hg0
  have := hfg.deriv_eq
  rw [deriv_id'', deriv_fun_mul (hg.differentiableAt.fun_pow 2) hh.differentiableAt,
    deriv_fun_pow hg.differentiableAt 2] at this
  simp [hg0] at this

/-- The function `z ↦ z ^ 2` is not reduced at `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 32]
theorem not_isReducedAt_sq : ¬ IsReducedAt (fun z : ℂ => z ^ 2) 0 := by
  intro H
  exact H (fun z => z) (fun _ => 1) analyticAt_id analyticAt_const
    (by filter_upwards with z; simp) rfl

/-- The zero function is not reduced at any point. -/
@[category test, AMS 14 32]
theorem not_isReducedAt_zero (p : E) : ¬ IsReducedAt (fun _ : E => (0 : ℂ)) p := by
  intro H
  exact H 0 0 analyticAt_const analyticAt_const
    (by filter_upwards with z; simp) rfl

/-- A set `W ⊆ ℂⁿ` is a *nonsingular (complex-analytic) subvariety of dimension `d`* near a
point `P ∈ W` if there is a biholomorphic chart of a neighbourhood of `P` in `ℂⁿ` onto an open
subset of `ℂ^d × ℂ^(n - d)` which carries `W` onto the linear subspace `ℂ^d × {0}`. -/
def IsSmoothSubvarietyAt {n : ℕ} (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ)
    (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ ψ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))),
    P ∈ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ ψ.source ∧ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ ψ.symm ψ.target ∧
      ∀ x ∈ ψ.source, x ∈ W ↔ (ψ x).2 = 0

/-- The hypersurface `V = {F = 0} ⊆ ℂⁿ` is *topologically equisingular* along the
`d`-dimensional subvariety `W` at the point `P ∈ W` if the triple `(ℂⁿ, V, W)` is locally
topologically trivial along `W` at `P`: there is a homeomorphism `h` from a neighbourhood `U` of
`P` in `ℂⁿ` onto a product `U₁ × U₂` of open sets `U₁ ⊆ ℂ^d`, `U₂ ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` such that
`h (W ∩ U) = U₁ × {0}` and `h (V ∩ U) = U₁ × S` for some set `S ⊆ ℂ^(n - d)` (so that `S ∩ U₂`
is homeomorphic to a transversal slice of `V`). Such an `h` yields, for every `Q ∈ W ∩ U`, a
homeomorphism between neighbourhoods of `Q` and `P` in `ℂⁿ` carrying `V` onto `V` and `Q` to `P`.
-/
def IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong {n : ℕ} (F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ)
    (W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))) (d : ℕ) (P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))
      (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d))))
    (U₁ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin d))) (U₂ S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (n - d)))),
    P ∈ h.source ∧ h.target = U₁ ×ˢ U₂ ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, x ∈ W ↔ (h x).2 = 0) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ h.source, F x = 0 ↔ (h x).2 ∈ S)

/-- **Zariski's multiplicity conjecture** (Zariski's Question A, [Za71]).

Let $f, g : (\mathbb{C}^n, 0) \to (\mathbb{C}, 0)$ be reduced holomorphic function germs, and
suppose that the hypersurface germs $(V(f), 0)$ and $(V(g), 0)$ have the same embedded
topological type, i.e. there is a homeomorphism $\varphi$ between open neighbourhoods of $0$ in
$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $\varphi(0) = 0$ carrying $V(f)$ onto $V(g)$. Then $f$ and $g$ have the same
multiplicity (order of vanishing) at $0$.

Here `φ` is an open partial homeomorphism of `ℂⁿ` whose source and target are neighbourhoods of
`0`; the hypothesis `hφ` says exactly that `φ` maps `V(f) ∩ φ.source` onto `V(g) ∩ φ.target`.
The reducedness hypotheses are essential: `f` and `f ^ 2` define the same zero set. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties {n : ℕ} {f g : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f 0) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g 0) (hf₀ : f 0 = 0) (hg₀ : g 0 = 0)
    (hf' : IsReducedAt f 0) (hg' : IsReducedAt g 0)
    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)))
    (h₀ : 0 ∈ φ.source) (hφ₀ : φ 0 = 0)
    (hφ : ∀ x ∈ φ.source, f x = 0 ↔ g (φ x) = 0) :
    orderAt f 0 = orderAt g 0 := by
  sorry

/-- **Topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity** (Zariski's Question B, [Za71]),
a consequence of `Varieties.varieties`.

Let $V = \{F = 0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a hypersurface with $F$ holomorphic and reduced at
$P \in V$, and let $W$ be a nonsingular subvariety of dimension $d$ through $P$. If $V$ is
topologically equisingular along $W$ at $P$, then $V$ is equimultiple along $W$ at $P$: the
multiplicity $m(V, Q)$ is constant for $Q \in W$ near $P$.

Topological equisingularity is taken in the sense of ambient local topological triviality of the
triple $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, W)$ along $W$ (see `IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong`), which is
stronger than asking that the germs $(\mathbb{C}^n, V, Q)$ have the same embedded topological
type for all $Q \in W$ near $P$. Topological equisingularity along $W$ together with $P \in V$
forces $W \subset V$ near $P$, so $W$ is a nonsingular subvariety of $V$ as in Zariski's
formulation. The conclusion is stated for `Q` in a neighbourhood of `P` in `W`, on which `F` is
holomorphic and reduced, so that `orderAt F Q` is the multiplicity of `V` at `Q`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 14 32]
theorem varieties.variants.equisingular_family {n d : ℕ} {F : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) → ℂ}
    {W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n))} {P : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)}
    (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F P) (hF₀ : F P = 0) (hF' : IsReducedAt F P)
    (hP : P ∈ W) (hW : IsSmoothSubvarietyAt W d P)
    (hV : IsTopologicallyEquisingularAlong F W d P) :
    ∀ᶠ Q in 𝓝[W] P, orderAt F Q = orderAt F P := by
  sorry

end Varieties

items: The Wikipedia background article (Algebraic variety) does not contain the conjecture; the precise formulation follows Zariski 1971 (Bull. AMS 77, Questions A and B) and Eyral's 2007 survey, in line with the decomposition notes.

ℂⁿ is modelled as `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n)`; ℂ^d × ℂ^(n-d) as a product of Euclidean spaces (product sup norm; topology and analyticity are norm-independent). `n - d` is truncated subtraction: for d > n the chart hypothesis is unsatisfiable, so the statement is vacuous there rather than wrong.

Multiplicity m(V,P) of the hypersurface V = {F = 0} at P is taken to be the order of the reduced defining function F at P (standard for hypersurfaces), formalised as the least k with `iteratedFDeriv ℂ k F P ≠ 0`, ℕ-valued with junk value 0 for the zero germ (excluded by `IsReducedAt`), mirroring Mathlib's `analyticOrderNatAt` convention.

Reducedness is square-freeness of the germ (no non-unit g with g² ∣ f in the germ ring), which also excludes f ≡ 0; analyticity of f is a separate hypothesis since `IsReducedAt` alone is vacuous for non-analytic f.

Slot 1: 'same embedded topological type' is an `OpenPartialHomeomorph` φ of ℂⁿ with 0 ∈ φ.source, φ 0 = 0 and ∀ x ∈ φ.source, f x = 0 ↔ g (φ x) = 0 (equivalent to φ(V(f) ∩ U) = V(g) ∩ U' since φ is a bijection source → target). The general n is stated; solved special cases (n = 2, C¹/bi-Lipschitz φ) are not included.

Slot 2: W is an arbitrary subset of ℂⁿ required to be a nonsingular d-dimensional analytic subvariety through P via a biholomorphic straightening chart (rather than fixing W to be a coordinate subspace), to stay literal to 'smooth subvariety W through P'.

Slot 2: topological equisingularity is fixed as ambient product triviality (Zariski's definition): homeomorphism onto U₁ × U₂ carrying W ∩ U onto U₁ × {0} and V ∩ U onto U₁ × S. No compatibility of h with a projection to W (fibre-preservation) is required, and S is an arbitrary set rather than required to be a hypersurface: both choices make the hypothesis weakest (hence the conjecture strongest) while keeping it a consequence of Question A (translation in the U₁ factor conjugated by h gives ambient homeomorphisms (ℂⁿ,V,Q) → (ℂⁿ,V,P) for Q ∈ W ∩ U). Requiring h(W∩U) = U₁ × {0} is essential: without it there are trivial counterexamples (e.g. V = {x² = y²} × ℂ with W a line inside one component).
Slot 2: W ⊂ V is not assumed explicitly; it follows from P ∈ V ∩ W and the product structure (0 ∈ S), as noted in the docstring.

Slot 2: the conclusion is 'for Q ∈ W near P' (`∀ᶠ Q in 𝓝[W] P`), since F is only assumed analytic and reduced at P (hence on a neighbourhood, where `orderAt F Q` equals m(V,Q)); the multiplicity used is that of V ⊂ ℂⁿ at Q (order of F as a function on ℂⁿ), not the order of a transversal slice function, matching Zariski's m(V,Q).
Added four proved `@[category test]` lemmas checking the bespoke `orderAt` and `IsReducedAt` on simple inputs (identity has order 1 and is reduced; z², 0 are not reduced).

reviewer_notes: The Wikipedia entry is a one-line list item; the supplied article (Algebraic variety) does not discuss the conjecture, so the precise content is Zariski's Questions A and B (Bull. AMS 1971) as fixed by the decomposition notes. Main ambiguity: the exact definition of 'topologically equisingular along W'. Candidates split among (a) transversal-section product (c03, c07), (b) fiber-preserving family trivialisation (c05, and with fiber-multiplicity conclusions c01, c02, c04, c06), and (c) general product triviality of the triple (ℂⁿ, V, W) with an arbitrary normal slice S (c08). All of (a)-(c) are implied by Question A; (c) has the weakest hypothesis and implies the others, matches the standard 'locally topologically trivial along W' language the notes prescribe, and keeps Zariski's conclusion m(V,Q) constant (multiplicity of V ⊂ ℂⁿ at Q, not of the slice f_t). If a reviewer prefers Zariski's transversal-section wording, c03/c07's version is a slightly weaker conjecture; the shipped one is strictly between Question A and that variant. c02 is provably false as formalised (FormalMultilinearSeries.order of a non-unique, possibly non-symmetric power series). Boundary cases: n = 0 or d = n make the hypotheses unsatisfiable (F ≡ 0 is not reduced); d = 0 makes the conclusion trivial; d > n is vacuous (no biholomorphic chart), all harmless. Both theorems posed as conjectures (positive answers) since the list entry calls it a conjecture.
